item.title: Ad hoc and Sensor Networks
item.description:
Ad hoc networks consist of a number of devices equipped with one or more wireless interfaces, which cooperate to provide wireless communications among them. Nodes which are not in the radio range of each other use other intermediate nodes as relays to find multi-hop paths towards a destination.

Unlike ad hoc networks, in sensor networks the devices are usually static. However, the way they work based on off, on and idle states, makes the topology variable. In addition, usually available resources are lesser, and the scalability of the solutions becomes a very important factor. This creates the need for localized algorithms rather than global or centralized ones.

item.title: Context-Aware Adaptive Multimedia
item.description:
Context Aware Adaptive applications are those who are able to modify and adapt their operation to their environment.

In particular, adaptive multimedia applications are a subset of those applications, which are able to adapt their internal components (e.g. audio and video codecs, rates, etc.) to maximize the user’s satisfaction in terms of perceived quality. To make that decision they use information from their environment called context.

item.title: Policy-Based Dynamic Management
item.description:
Network, service and application management today faces numerous challenges, ones that older ways of doing things cannot solve. The concept of policy-based management (PBM) addresses some of these problems and offers possible solutions.

It provides a system-wide view of the network and its services and applications, and shifts the emphasis of network management and monitoring away from specific devices and interfaces towards users and applications.

item.title: Intelligent Transportation Systems
item.description: The work on Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) is especially focused on navigation systems in general and location-based services, GNSS and inertial navigation, data fusion in road vehicle applications, mobile communications, vehicle communication, and electronic vehicle identification.

item.title: Optimization and Intelligent Data Analysis
item.description: The objective of this line is extracting useful knowledge from large volumes of information. We design and improve techniques of Data Intelligent Analysis and of Optimization to apply them to real problems of the logistic, economic-financial, bioinformatics type. The obtained models serve to understand better the behaviour of the problems and act in a more real way.

item.title: Ambient Intelligent and Ubiquitous Computing
item.description: This line is focused on the study of techniques for coordination and adaptiveness of ubiquitous services. In this manner, complex systems composed by a large number of autonomous entities coordinate in a suitable manner. Besides, adaptiveness of such autonomous entities is studied — they are modelled by means of behaviour patterns.

item.title: Advanced Security Services and AAA
item.description:
Today there exist different solutions and services related with security, but they are highly heterogeneous and it is impossible to ensure a global and homogeneous system security solution.

The definition of frameworks able to combine coherently some of the current security technologies, services and protocols seems to be a real need for current and next-generation information systems.

item.title: NEMESIS lanza una convocatoria para fortalecer y ampliar su red de parcelas experimentales para la salud del suelo en el Mediterráneo
item.description: Los solicitantes seleccionados recibirán financiación y se integrarán en los Living Labs para desarrollar y probar soluciones frente a la degradación del suelo.

item.title: La Cátedra OSIRIS organiza en la Universidad de Murcia el seminario internacional “Eyes on the Road”
item.description: El encuentro reunió expertos en visión por computador y Edge AI para mostrar cómo transformar datos de tráfico urbano en inteligencia útil para ciudades más eficientes.

item.title: Ciencia y tecnología para la agricultura sostenible en la II Feria Científica de Santomera
item.description: Los proyectos OSIRIS y NEMESIS acercaron la investigación en agricultura digital y salud del suelo al público joven durante la II Feria Científica de Santomera.

item.title: Investigadores del proyecto OSIRIS participan en el Máster en Big Data de la Universidad de Murcia
item.description: Los investigadores Adrián Cánovas Rodríguez y Yu Ye presentaron casos de uso de inteligencia artificial y análisis de datos aplicados a agricultura y medio ambiente en el Máster en Big Data de la Universidad de Murcia.

item.title: La Universidad de Sofía visita la Universidad de Murcia para conocer los avances del proyecto OSIRIS
item.description: La Cátedra OSIRIS mostró cómo la combinación de inteligencia artificial, sensorización avanzada e imágenes satelitales permite gestionar cultivos de forma más eficiente y sostenible, a partir de los desarrollos que se están aplicando en su invernadero experimental y plataforma de control inteligente.

item.title: La Cátedra Osiris presenta en MobiSec 2025 un innovador sistema de aprendizaje federado para riego inteligente en entornos agrícolas semiáridos
item.description: Presentado en Sapporo un sistema de aprendizaje federado embebido que combina IA, eficiencia energética y protección de datos para optimizar el riego en zonas semiáridas. Validado en parcelas de la Región de Murcia, demuestra su viabilidad en dispositivos autónomos alimentados por energía solar.

item.title: La UMU presenta en la ExcellCity Winter School 2025 sus avances en el uso de imágenes satelitales para una agricultura más sostenible
item.description: La Cátedra OSIRIS mostró en Sofía (Bulgaria) cómo la combinación de imágenes Sentinel-2, datos climáticos y modelos de IA permite monitorizar cultivos en tiempo real y optimizar el uso del agua, con resultados obtenidos en parcelas de la Región de Murcia.

item.title: NEMESIS: a new Horizon Europe project to restore Mediterranean soils
item.description: The NEMESIS project, funded by Horizon Europe, aims to combat desertification and restore soil health in vulnerable Mediterranean regions through five interconnected Living Labs. The University of Murcia joins an international consortium working on sustainable, community-driven soil solutions.
